column1: # Hand-made file boundaries and names, merged by tools/split_files.py.
# A row forces a file to start at `text` with this name (renaming the
# generated file if one already starts there); if the generator started a
# file with this name elsewhere, that start is dropped, so a row can move a
# file's start. `rodata` forces where its .rodata starts ('-': inferred).

column4: Moves the start from 0x101CCC. 0x101CCC-0x102488 read the pad through BedPad's socket (+0x20: scePad2GetState, scePad2Read) and fill or read BedPad fields (sticks at +0x7E..+0x81, floats at +0x4C..+0x58), calling each other: BedPad methods, so they end bed/bedpad. 0x102490 is the first function that touches no BedPad (looks up a game table, like the utl/utlgame.cpp functions after it).

Moves the start from 0x100320. That function zeroes m_depth (+0x50) and m_stack (+0x10..+0x4F), BedSubMode's exact layout, and its only caller is the constructor at 0x1360A0 (mag/magscene2), right after zeroing that member's m_cur and m_stack inline: it is a BedSubMode method, so it ends bed/bedsubmode. 0x100354 is the first function with bed/bedmemory.cpp asserts.

Moves the start from 0x101718. That function zeroes a 0x1C-byte object whose fields (+0x00..+0x18) are the heap object bed/bedmemory works on (0x100354 initialises the same fields) and is only called from a static initialiser, on the global heap later passed to bedmemory's allocator 0x100C84: it is bedmemory's heap constructor. 0x101738 is BedPfh::clear, called by 0x101750 (the first function with bed/bedpfh asserts) and by every BedPfh user right before it.
Engine graphics library (C): I3D_BIN/I3D_I3M/I3D_I3C format IDs in its .rodata; called from dog/, mag/, effects and menus. Every function is 8-aligned (built with other flags than the game).
Sound library: from here on callers are snd/ and game/ (sound manager); 0x237D00 is the first function calling into this region, the ones before it are called by i3d.

The functions between utlIsTcc (utl/utlmisc) and utl/utlfile: VU0 vftoi15 helpers, a text tokenizer, a frame counter (0x105B3C, the only user of the first .data word, 0x295F00), the global operator new/delete and wrappers of the global heap (the BedMemory at 0x6E9800). No assert or .rodata names them; they may be the tail of utl/utlmisc or several files.

Moves the start from 0x1056E8. The asserts of 0x105E50 are at utl/utlfile.cpp lines 15-16 (those of 0x105F0C at 36-37), so it is the file's first function: lines 1-12 leave no room for another. Only these two functions use the file's .rodata (0x2E7760).

Moves the start from 0x106010. 0x1060E8 has the first utl/utlfind.cpp assert, at line 22, and the next functions assert every 12-14 lines: no room for two functions before it. The two before it are generic string helpers (a case-insensitive compare called from mag/magloader, a bounded upper-case copy called from debug/motnamecnv, with utlStrCopy's parameters), so they end utl/utlfile; the rest of utl/utlfind serves MagLifeBwnCtrl.

The functions between utl/utlfind and DogMotionBlend's methods: a sound-id lookup for SndMan (the only user of the .data table at 0x295F08), a wrapper around an i3d call, and vector/angle math over sceVu0 and atanf, called from dog/, mag/ and effects. No assert or .rodata names them; they may be the tail of utl/utlfind or several files.

Moves the start from 0x106658. 0x10737C is the first function that works on a DogMotionBlend (m_main at +0x00, m_motion at +0x1C, like 0x107560, whose asserts at dog/dogmotionblend.cpp lines 83-87 name those fields); every function before it is unrelated math, sound or i3d code.

Moves the start from 0x10F5E4. 0x10F860 has the first dog/dogcamera.cpp assert, at line 22; the functions before it are DogActor's eye methods (unk/0010F3A4), whose float table at 0x2E84B0 comes right before the "dog/dogcamera.cpp" string (0x2E84C0) that starts dogcamera's .rodata.

Moves the start from 0x108588. 0x108588 is DogMotionBlend's constructor (the reset values of DogMotionBlend::validate, plus m_speedRatio = 1 and m_tickTime = -1), right after DogMotionBlend's last method; DogActor's constructors call it for their two DogMotionBlend members (+0x1E4, +0x2C4). It ends dog/dogmotionblend.

DogActor's eye methods (material lookup by the name "eye", blinking: fields +0x470..+0x494). Their .rodata ("eye" at 0x2E8488, the frame tables at 0x2E8490 and 0x2E84B0) comes after the RTTI names ("9DogEntity", "8DogActor") and the asserts of DogActor's inline methods (getMotion, getBlendMotion), which end dog/dogactor's .rodata because a translation unit emits them last: they are a file of their own. 0x10F2DC, right before, asserts at dog/dogactor.cpp line 4614.
